name: CoQ10 for gums

lead: CoQ10 is a compound the body makes and that is sold as a supplement. It is taken or applied as an extra to reduce gum inflammation, with calmer, healthier-looking gums as the goal.

It works in cellular energy production and as an antioxidant, which is the rationale for gum use. Registered trials exist, including CoQ10 with probiotics during periodontal treatment in pregnancy, but no results were found. General evidence for CoQ10 supplements is limited and mixed, and the US FDA has not approved it for any medical condition.

paras: It is used as a supplement or a gum-applied product alongside regular periodontal treatment and home care, not in place of them.
Generally well tolerated; nausea and headache are reported, and it may reduce the effect of warfarin, so anyone on blood thinners would check with a clinician.

angle.text: CoQ10 is used as an antioxidant add-on to ease gum inflammation, aiming for calmer, healthier gums alongside periodontal care. Trials are registered, but published results were not found.

lead: Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10, ubiquinone) is a fat-soluble compound made by the body and sold as a supplement; it is studied as an adjunct therapy to reduce inflammation in periodontitis.[1]

General evidence for CoQ10 supplements is limited and mixed, and the US FDA has not approved it for any medical condition.[1] Registered trials examine CoQ10 with probiotics during periodontal treatment in pregnancy.[2][3] No results were found.

paras: CoQ10 acts in mitochondrial energy production and as an antioxidant, and is found in meat, fish and oils.[1] It is generally well tolerated, with nausea and headache reported, and it may interact with warfarin.[1]

Two registered trials, recruiting or enrolling, test CoQ10 combined with probiotics as an adjunct in periodontal therapy for pregnant women.[2][3] Published results were not found. A pilot trial of an oil rinse product is also registered.[4]

timeline.event: CoQ10 isolated from beef heart mitochondria.[1]
